욥기-15-1.title: 욥기 15장 1절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-15-1.exegesis: 22. "Flesh" and "soul" describe the whole man. Scripture rests the hope of a future life, not on the inherent immortality of the soul, but on the restoration of the body with the soul. In the unseen world, Job in a gloomy frame anticipates, man shall be limited to the thought of his own misery. "Pain is by personification, from our feelings while alive, attributed to the flesh and soul, as if the man could feel in his body when dead. It is the dead in general, not the wicked, who are meant here."

욥기-15-3.title: 욥기 15장 3절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-15-3.exegesis: CHAPTER 15 SECOND SERIES. Job 15:1-35 . Second Speech of Eliphaz. 2. a wise man-- which Job claims to be. vain knowledge-- Hebrew, "windy knowledge"; literally, "of wind" ( Job 8:2 ). In Ec 1:14 , Hebrew, "to catch wind," expresses to strive for what is vain. east wind-- stronger than the previous "wind," for in that region the east wind is the most destructive of winds ( Is 27:8 ). Thus here,--empty violence. belly-- the inward parts, the breast ( Pr 18:8 ).

욥기-15-5.title: 욥기 15장 5절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-15-5.exegesis: 4. fear-- reverence for God ( Job 4:6 ; Psa 2:11 ). prayer-- meditation, in Psa 104:34 ; so devotion. If thy views were right, reasons Eliphaz, that God disregards the afflictions of the righteous and makes the wicked to prosper, all devotion would be at an end.

욥기-15-6.exegesis: 5. The sophistry of thine own speeches proves thy guilt.
욥기-15-6.theologicalNote: 5. The sophistry of thine own speeches proves thy guilt.

욥기-15-7.title: 욥기 15장 7절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-15-7.exegesis: 6. No pious man would utter such sentiments.
욥기-15-7.theologicalNote: 6. No pious man would utter such sentiments.

욥기-15-8.title: 욥기 15장 8절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-15-8.exegesis: 7. That is, Art thou wisdom personified? Wisdom existed before the hills; that is, the eternal Son of God ( Pr 8:25 ; Psa 90:2 ). Wast thou in existence before Adam? The farther back one existed, the nearer he was to the Eternal Wisdom.

욥기-15-9.title: 욥기 15장 9절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-15-9.exegesis: 8. secret-- rather, "Wast thou a listener in the secret council of God?" The Hebrew means properly the cushions of a divan on which counsellors in the East usually sit. God's servants are admitted to God's secrets ( Psa 25:14 ; Ge 18:17 ; Joh 15:15 ). restrain-- Rather, didst thou take away, or borrow, thence (namely, from the divine secret council) thy wisdom? Eliphaz in this ( Job 15:8 , 9 ) retorts Job's words upon himself ( Job 12:2 , 3 ; 13:2 ).

욥기-15-10.title: 욥기 15장 10절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-15-10.exegesis: 9. in us-- or, "with us," Hebraism for "we are aware of."
욥기-15-10.theologicalNote: 9. in us-- or, "with us," Hebraism for "we are aware of."

욥기-15-11.title: 욥기 15장 11절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-15-11.exegesis: 10. On our side, thinking with us are the aged. Job had admitted that wisdom is with them ( Job 12:12 ). Eliphaz seems to have been himself older than Job; perhaps the other two were also ( Job 32:6 ). Job, in Job 30:1 , does not refer to his three friends; it therefore forms no objection. The Arabs are proud of fulness of years.

욥기-15-12.title: 욥기 15장 12절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-15-12.exegesis: 11. consolations-- namely, the revelation which Eliphaz had stated as a consolatory reproof to Job, and which he repeats in Job 15:14 . secret-- Hast thou some secret wisdom and source of consolation, which makes thee disregard those suggested by me? ( Job 15:8 ). Rather, from a different Hebrew root, Is the word of kindness or gentleness addressed by me treated by thee as valueless? [Umbreit].

욥기-15-13.title: 욥기 15장 13절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-15-13.exegesis: 12. wink-- that is, why do thy eyes evince pride? ( Pr 6:13 ; Psa 35:19 ).
욥기-15-13.theologicalNote: 12. wink-- that is, why do thy eyes evince pride? ( Pr 6:13 ; Psa 35:19 ).

욥기-15-14.title: 욥기 15장 14절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-15-14.exegesis: 13. That is, frettest against God and lettest fall rash words.
욥기-15-14.theologicalNote: 13. That is, frettest against God and lettest fall rash words.

욥기-15-15.title: 욥기 15장 15절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-15-15.exegesis: 14. Eliphaz repeats the revelation ( Job 4:17 ) in substance, but using Job's own words (see on Job 14:1 , on "born of a woman") to strike him with his own weapons.
욥기-15-15.theologicalNote: 14. Eliphaz repeats the revelation ( Job 4:17 ) in substance, but using Job's own words (see on Job 14:1 , on "born of a woman") to strike him with his own weapons.

욥기-15-16.title: 욥기 15장 16절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-15-16.exegesis: 15. Repeated from Job 4:18 ; "servants" there are "saints" here; namely, holy angels. heavens-- literally, or else answering to "angels" (see on Job 4:18 , and Job 25:5 ).

욥기-15-17.title: 욥기 15장 17절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-15-17.exegesis: 16. filthy-- in Arabic "sour" ( Psa 14:3 ; 53:3 ), corrupted from his original purity. drinketh-- ( Pr 19:28 ).
욥기-15-17.theologicalNote: 16. filthy-- in Arabic "sour" ( Psa 14:3 ; 53:3 ), corrupted from his original purity. drinketh-- ( Pr 19:28 ).

욥기-15-18.title: 욥기 15장 18절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-15-18.exegesis: 17. In direct contradiction of Job's position ( Job 12:6 , &c.), that the lot of the wicked was the most prosperous here, Eliphaz appeals (1) to his own experience, (2) to the wisdom of the ancients.

욥기-15-19.title: 욥기 15장 19절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-15-19.exegesis: 18. Rather, "and which as handed down from their fathers, they have not concealed."
욥기-15-19.theologicalNote: 18. Rather, "and which as handed down from their fathers, they have not concealed."

욥기-15-20.title: 욥기 15장 20절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-15-20.exegesis: 19. Eliphaz speaks like a genuine Arab when he boasts that his ancestors had ever possessed the land unmixed with foreigners [Umbreit]. His words are intended to oppose Job's ( Job 9:24 ); "the earth" in their case was not "given into the hand of the wicked." He refers to the division of the earth by divine appointment ( Ge 10:5 ; 25:32 ). Also he may insinuate that Job's sentiments had been corrupted from original purity by his vicinity to the Sabeans and Chaldeans [Rosenmuller].

욥기-15-21.title: 욥기 15장 21절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-15-21.exegesis: 20. travaileth-- rather, "trembleth of himself," though there is no real danger [Umbreit]. and the number of his years, &c.-- This gives the reason why the wicked man trembles continually; namely, because he knows not the moment when his life must end.

욥기-15-22.title: 욥기 15장 22절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-15-22.exegesis: 21. An evil conscience conceives alarm at every sudden sound, though it be in a time of peace ("prosperity"), when there is no real danger ( Le 26:36 ; Pr 28:1 ; 2Ki 7:6 ).
욥기-15-22.theologicalNote: 21. An evil conscience conceives alarm at every sudden sound, though it be in a time of peace ("prosperity"), when there is no real danger ( Le 26:36 ; Pr 28:1 ; 2Ki 7:6 ).

욥기-15-23.title: 욥기 15장 23절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-15-23.exegesis: 22. darkness-- namely, danger or calamity. Glancing at Job, who despaired of restoration: in contrast to good men when in darkness ( Mi 7:8 , 9 ). waited for of-- that is, He is destined for the sword [Gesenius]. Rather (in the night of danger), "he looks anxiously towards the sword," as if every sword was drawn against him [Umbreit].

욥기-15-24.title: 욥기 15장 24절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-15-24.exegesis: 23. Wandereth in anxious search for bread. Famine in Old Testament depicts sore need ( Is 5:13 ). Contrast the pious man's lot ( Job 5:20-22 ). knoweth-- has the firm conviction. Contrast the same word applied to the pious ( Job 5:24 , 25 ). ready at his hand-- an Arabic phrase to denote a thing's complete readiness and full presence, as if in the hand.

욥기-15-25.title: 욥기 15장 25절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-15-25.exegesis: 24. prevail-- break upon him suddenly and terribly, as a king, &c. ( Pr 6:11 ).
욥기-15-25.theologicalNote: 24. prevail-- break upon him suddenly and terribly, as a king, &c. ( Pr 6:11 ).

욥기-15-26.title: 욥기 15장 26절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-15-26.exegesis: 25. stretcheth ... hand-- wielding the spear, as a bold rebel against God ( Job 9:4 ; Is 27:4 ).
욥기-15-26.theologicalNote: 25. stretcheth ... hand-- wielding the spear, as a bold rebel against God ( Job 9:4 ; Is 27:4 ).

욥기-15-27.title: 욥기 15장 27절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-15-27.exegesis: 26. on his neck-- rather, "with outstretched neck," namely, that of the rebel [Umbreit] ( Psa 75:5 ). upon ... bucklers-- rather, "with--his (the rebel's, not God's) bucklers." The rebel and his fellows are depicted as joining shields together, to form a compact covering over their heads against the weapons hurled on them from a fortress [Umbreit and Gesenius].

욥기-15-28.title: 욥기 15장 28절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-15-28.exegesis: 27. The well-nourished body of the rebel is the sign of his prosperity. collops-- masses of fat. He pampers and fattens himself with sensual indulgences; hence his rebellion against God ( De 32:15 ; 1Sa 2:29 ).

욥기-15-29.title: 욥기 15장 29절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-15-29.exegesis: 28. The class of wicked here described is that of robbers who plunder "cities," and seize on the houses of the banished citizens ( Is 13:20 ). Eliphaz chooses this class because Job had chosen the same ( Job 12:6 ). heaps-- of ruins.

욥기-15-30.title: 욥기 15장 30절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-15-30.exegesis: 29. Rather, he shall not increase his riches; he has reached his highest point; his prosperity shall not continue. perfection-- rather, "His acquired wealth--what he possesses--shall not be extended," &c.
욥기-15-30.theologicalNote: 29. Rather, he shall not increase his riches; he has reached his highest point; his prosperity shall not continue. perfection-- rather, "His acquired wealth--what he possesses--shall not be extended," &c.

욥기-15-31.title: 욥기 15장 31절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-15-31.exegesis: 30. depart-- that is, escape ( Job 15:22 , 23 ). branches-- namely, his offspring ( Job 1:18 , 19 ; Psa 37:35 ). dry up-- The "flame" is the sultry wind in the East by which plants most full of sap are suddenly shrivelled. his mouth-- that is, God's wrath ( Is 11:4 ).

욥기-15-32.title: 욥기 15장 32절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-15-32.exegesis: 31. Rather, "let him not trust in vanity or he will be deceived," &c. vanity-- that which is unsubstantial. Sin is its own punishment ( Pr 1:31 ; Jr 2:19 ).
욥기-15-32.theologicalNote: 31. Rather, "let him not trust in vanity or he will be deceived," &c. vanity-- that which is unsubstantial. Sin is its own punishment ( Pr 1:31 ; Jr 2:19 ).

욥기-15-33.title: 욥기 15장 33절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-15-33.exegesis: 32. Literally, "it (the tree to which he is compared, Job 15:30 , or else his life) shall not be filled up in its time"; that is, "he shall be ended before his time." shall not be green-- image from a withered tree; the childless extinction of the wicked.

욥기-15-34.title: 욥기 15장 34절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-15-34.exegesis: 33. Images of incompleteness. The loss of the unripe grapes is poetically made the vine tree's own act, in order to express more pointedly that the sinner's ruin is the fruit of his own conduct ( Is 3:11 ; Jr 6:19 ).

욥기-15-35.title: 욥기 15장 35절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-15-35.exegesis: 34. Rather, The binding together of the hypocrites (wicked) shall be fruitless [Umbreit]. tabernacles of bribery-- namely, dwellings of unjust judges, often reprobated in the Old Testament ( Is 1:23 ). The "fire of God" that consumed Job's possessions ( Job 1:16 ) Eliphaz insinuates may have been on account of Job's bribery as an Arab sheik or emir.
